answers.answer: No fabrication, but the question exposes a real labeling tension I must state precisely. My spec cleanly separates two objects: (a) the labeled COST BAND ~$0.25-1.80/garment (A1 ~$0.30-0.90, A2 ~$0.25-0.70, A3 ~$0.60-1.80), method = triangulated process-reasoning, NOT a vendor quote [ESTIMATE], and (b) the per-piece Ludhiana finishing JOB-WORK RATE at a NAMED finisher, which is [UNKNOWN] and is my highest-priority T4 blocker (JOBWORK_RATE_BLOCKER, kb2/kb3). These are not the same input: the band is a planning triangulation whose ORDERING (A3>A1>A2) is sound but whose ABSOLUTE numbers are explicitly placeholders that 'must NOT be fed as points into the T4 model without a live quote' (COST_BENCHMARK_HONESTY). So quoting the band is not fabricating precision around the blocker PROVIDED I (1) carry the [ESTIMATE] tag with method+basis, (2) never present the band as decision-usable at point precision, and (3) keep the per-piece rate itself [UNKNOWN] and named as the blocker. My escalation_triggers[0] enforces exactly this: 'the triangulated bands must not be fed as points into the downstream economics model and the rate is named as the blocker.' The honest gap: my spec gives the band a range but does NOT publish the full method+basis+confidence derivation inline, so a downstream reader could over-trust it; the fix is to keep emphasizing ordering-sound / magnitude-placeholder and let unit_economics (T4/T9) refuse it as a point.
answers.grounded_in: kb2 COST_BENCHMARK_HONESTY (the ~$0.25-1.80 band, A3>A1>A2, 'ABSOLUTE numbers are placeholders that must NOT be fed as points'); kb2/kb3 JOBWORK_RATE_BLOCKER (per-garment rate [UNKNOWN], highest-priority T4 blocker, never fabricated); spec boundaries[0]; escalation_triggers[0]; conflicts_and_dominance 'labeled-estimate honesty versus a decisive recipe'; router N1/N2.
answers.gap_note: The distinction between the labeled cost BAND and the [UNKNOWN] per-piece RATE is fully in-spec, but the spec does not carry an explicit method+basis+confidence derivation string for the $-band inline; it relies on the 'ordering sound / absolute placeholder / do-not-feed-as-points' guard. That guard holds honesty, but a downstream consumer could still over-read the band as harder than the rate beneath it, so the item is a watch/soften-language finding, not a clean pass.

answers.answer: I do NOT answer the money/viability question in-lane, and my 'finishing is cheap, gate is decisive' framing must not imply a naive GO. Correct handling: viability = does the venture make money is owned by unit_economics_strategist + the DECISION_MEMO (router dominance rule on viability), decided on contribution-margin-after-CAC (LTV:CAC > ~3), NOT on factory or finishing cost. So I answer only my slice: the A1 gas-singe + cellulase bio-polish recipe is a labeled MINORITY cost slice (A1 ~$0.30-0.90/garment [ESTIMATE]) and finishing PRICE is not the binding constraint; the QUALITY GATE is (COST_OF_QUALITY_TRADE). I then DEFER the money verdict and carry the GATED-conditional-GO posture with the four hard gates: G1 live blended CAC <~$35 organic-led [UNKNOWN], G2 knit+LINK job-work rate [UNKNOWN], G3 working-capital funding [UNSIZED], G4 anti-pill PPS ICI >=3-4 post-wash [UNKNOWN]. My own finishing G4 contribution is real (the eight-check post-wash gate is the garment-side half of that anti-pill gate) but even a passing A1 recipe does not make the venture money; inventory cash stays FORBIDDEN until G1-G4 pass (N7). 'Finishing is a small slice' means finishing is NOT where the venture lives or dies, NOT that spending on it is a GO.
answers.grounded_in: kb3 COST_OF_QUALITY_TRADE (finishing price minority slice, gate is the binding constraint); spec capability 'merge into a labeled-estimate per-article finishing go/no-go'; router dominance_rules 'viability -> unit_economics + DECISION_MEMO'; macro.the_four_hard_gates; neutralize_gate N6/N7.

answers.answer: No, I cannot deliver ICI >=3-4 on a cheap high-pill A2 acrylic 'at finishing,' and this is exactly where I refuse the single most expensive spec lie. Acrylic is THERMOPLASTIC (a flame beads/melts it, so it cannot be cleanly singed) and NON-CELLULOSIC (cellulase does nothing), so the ONLY finishing option on A2 is a chemical/silicone top-up worth a FRACTION of a grade [ESTIMATE: industry-lore, MED-HIGH], and how much that fraction actually buys on our exact construction is [UNKNOWN] (direction: small). The blunt rule from A2_ACRYLIC_RECIPE and CHEMICAL_ANTIPILL: A2's ICI grade is WON OR LOST AT THE YARN PO (anti-pill/high-dpf grade, higher twist, 2-ply, tight gauge), NOT on the finishing line. The line I draw: if the yarn floor is set (yarn PO already specs an anti-pill/high-dpf acrylic to ICI >=3-4 post-wash) finishing adds a light silicone top-up plus an under-set press and relax/compact. If the yarn is cheap/high-pill, the fix is to RE-OPEN THE YARN SPEC, not pile on chemical anti-pill; a freshly-softened showroom sample that pills one wash later is the expensive spec lie (escalation_triggers 'a recipe/showroom sample claims finishing will fix a high-pill yarn -> flag'). This is a viability-adjacent hard gate (G4), on which pilling dominance says yarn_sourcing sets the FLOOR and finishing is the SECOND line, so I defer the floor to yarn and refuse the rescue.
answers.grounded_in: kb2 A2_ACRYLIC_RECIPE ('win it upstream, finish light'; won-or-lost-at-the-yarn-PO; re-open the yarn spec); kb1 CHEMICAL_ANTIPILL (acrylic primary, fraction of a grade, magnitude [UNKNOWN]); spec boundaries[1]; conflicts_and_dominance 'yarn-PO floor versus finishing ceiling'; router pilling dominance rule + N7 gate G4.

answers.answer: No contradiction, and the magnitudes are held [UNKNOWN], not asserted. The reconciliation is that 'second line of defence' and 'earns a real grade on A1' are about DIFFERENT fibres and DIFFERENT mechanisms, and in BOTH cases the yarn floor still dominates. On A1 COTTON, finishing has real cellulosic chemistry to work with (gas-singe removes surface fuzz at the yarn stage; cellulase bio-polish hydrolyses protruding cellulosic micro-fibrils and light abrasion snaps them off), so finishing earns a REAL, ownable, wash-durable anti-pill grade [ESTIMATE: process-reasoning, direction HIGH]. On A2 ACRYLIC, the fibre is thermoplastic and non-cellulosic, so those mechanisms do not apply and finishing buys only a chemical/silicone FRACTION. On A3 WOOL, milling/boarding craft plus a few-% nylon upstream carry it to ICI >=4. Critically, I hold the DIRECTIONS HIGH and the MAGNITUDES LOW: the exact number of ICI grades finishing adds on any construction is [UNKNOWN] until PPS swatch testing (PILLING_GATE_POSTWASH: 'per-route ICI-grade uplift on our exact constructions is UNKNOWN until PPS swatch testing; keep the directions HIGH but the magnitudes LOW'; escalation_triggers 'uplift asserted as a magnitude -> defer'). So I do not claim '+1.0 grade on A1' or '+0.25 on A2'; I claim a directional real-grade-vs-fraction split and defer magnitude to the swatch. The yarn floor dominating means even A1's real grade builds ON the yarn PO floor, never replaces a cheap yarn.
answers.grounded_in: kb3 FINISHING_AS_SECOND_DEFENCE + FINISHING_EFFICACY_FORMULA (A1 high / A2 fractional / A3 craft-dependent, directions HIGH magnitudes LOW); kb3 PILLING_GATE_POSTWASH (per-construction uplift [UNKNOWN] until PPS); kb1 ANTIPILL_ROUTE_MAP + BIOPOLISH_CELLULASE; spec escalation_triggers 'ICI-grade uplift asserted as a magnitude -> defer'; router N4/N6.

answers.answer: I give the owner a felt/area-shrink GATE, not a machine setpoint, and I refuse to hand the ~39-41 C / 8-12 min window as a setting. Milling/fulling is wool-only, is the same physics as accidental shrink-felting deliberately stopped at a target, and is IRREVERSIBLE if over-done -- the single most destructive finishing failure (MILLING_FULLING, MILLING_GATE). Therefore it is gated on DIMENSIONS + a FELT/AREA-SHRINK LIMIT + HAND, NEVER to the clock; time is only the short dial (minutes). The cited ~39-41 C / 8-12 min is explicitly [ESTIMATE: industry-lore, single-source, MED -- order-of-magnitude only] and my spec's own con says it 'cannot be quoted as a recipe setpoint.' So the deliverable for an A3 merino lot is: (1) set the ACCEPTANCE target = the tech-pack area-shrink/felt limit + target hand, (2) dial the machine in at SAMPLING/PPS, stopping on the measured felt/area-shrink target not a minute count, (3) treat the temp/time only as a starting band to converge from. I also flag that milling capacity + felt-control reliability in-cluster is [UNKNOWN] (A3 low-volume, possibly seasonal), and route the actual setpoint to a specialist wool finisher (outsource-all-wet). Handing ~40 C / 10 min as a setpoint would be fake precision on an irreversible step and risks a scrapped premium lot on the first bulk run.
answers.grounded_in: kb1 MILLING_FULLING ('~39-41 C / 8-12 min' flagged single-source order-of-magnitude; gated on felt/area-shrink limit not the clock; irreversible); kb2 MILLING_GATE + A3_WOOL_RECIPE (milling time = irreversible pass/fail dial, gated on felt/area-shrink limit; outsource to a specialist wool finisher); spec conflicts_and_dominance 'milling for a fuller softer hand versus irreversible felting'; escalation_triggers 'uplift/settings asserted as magnitude -> defer'.

(2) Name -- not adjudicate -- the regulated boundary: owning ANY wet node imports regulated-effluent exposure (cluster CETP non-compliance, CPCB-penalty, NGT-closure risk) out of proportion to a three-article line; this is inherited from the T1 never-own-a-dyehouse boundary and I must NOT contradict it or invent the effluent-compliance cost (which stays [UNKNOWN] on my side). answers.answer: Honest concession: the same-gate-on-both-POs mechanism GUARANTEES both ends are tested and that a skipped step cannot pass on the other vendor's test, but it does NOT by itself fully ADJUDICATE fault when a post-wash pilling fail could be either the yarn floor or a skipped/under-dosed bio-polish -- there is a hand-off seam. My spec even names this con: 'Two POs add a hand-off seam where responsibility for a failed gate can be disputed' (TWO_PO_STRUCTURE cons). The partial disambiguator I DO have: on A1 the RETAINED bursting/tensile strength check (gate check 4, mandatory after bio-polish) distinguishes an over-dosed/under-dosed bio-polish (strength moves) from a yarn-floor pilling failure (strength intact but pills). Spirality similarly fingers an upstream unbalanced-ply yarn dial, not finishing (SPIRALITY_SISTER_FAULT). But for a pure pilling fail at grade 3 with strength intact, my 'yarn floor dominates' rule does bias toward re-opening the yarn PO, and I concede that is a DIRECTION of adjudication, not a per-vendor contractual fault-assignment mechanism. The gap is real: my spec specifies the shared gate and the strength check but does not fully specify a per-PO fault-attribution / arbitration clause (e.g. requiring a retained-strength + hairiness read on BOTH the yarn lot and the finished garment so the delta localizes the defect). That is a 'propose' improvement, honestly flagged, not something I should invent as already-solved.
answers.grounded_in: kb2 TWO_PO_STRUCTURE (shared gate; cons: hand-off seam where fault can be disputed); kb3 TWO_PO_RECIPE + ACCEPTANCE_GATE_EIGHT_CHECKS (check 4 retained strength A1-mandatory; both-ends testing rationale); kb3 SPIRALITY_SISTER_FAULT (gate reads but cannot fix a yarn-floor fault); spec conflicts_and_dominance 'yarn-PO floor versus finishing ceiling'.
answers.gap_note: The shared-gate mechanism closes the 'skipped step passes at the wrong vendor' hole and the retained-strength/spirality checks partially localize a mixed failure, but the spec does not carry an explicit per-PO fault-attribution/arbitration clause for a pure pilling fail with strength intact; 'yarn floor dominates' is a direction, not a contractual adjudicator. Genuine gap -> propose adding a both-ends retained-strength + hairiness read so the delta localizes fault; do not claim it is already specified.

answers.answer: Honest gap: my anti-pill route identities are stated for the PURE fibre chemistry, and the line is built on BLENDS, so the mapping needs a blend caveat my spec only partially carries. The process identities I hold as FACT are fibre-fraction-specific, and that is actually the right primitive: (a) cellulase acts on the CELLULOSIC fraction only -- on an A1 cotton/acrylic or cotton/poly blend it de-fuzzes the cotton and does NOTHING to the synthetic fraction, so a high-synthetic-fraction A1 gets less bio-polish benefit and the synthetic fraction's pilling must be handled upstream (fibre/twist/nylon), not by cellulase. (b) Gas-singeing on a blend: the flame cleans the cotton fuzz but on the THERMOPLASTIC fraction a flame beads/melts rather than cleanly singes (GASSING_SINGEING: 'does NOT work on acrylic... beads/melts'), so singeing a high-thermoplastic blend risks beading the synthetic component -- singe fits cotton-RICH/viscose blends, and a blend with meaningful acrylic/poly must be assessed, not assumed singe-able. (c) Milling acts on the WOOL fraction; A3 is merino/lambswool with a few-% nylon -- nylon is non-felting so it rides through milling as the abrasion/pill lever while the wool fraction felts; milling still gated on felt/area-shrink. So the clean 'cellulase=cellulosics-only, singe=cotton, mill=wool' mapping does NOT silently break -- it correctly generalizes as FRACTION-specific -- BUT my spec states the routes on the pure-fibre archetype and does not spell out the blend-fraction behaviour inline for each shipping article. That is a real coverage gap on the exact blended articles.
answers.grounded_in: kb1 BIOPOLISH_CELLULASE (cellulosics-only, does nothing on acrylic/wool); kb1 GASSING_SINGEING (cotton/cellulosic; beads/melts on thermoplastic; fits cotton-rich/viscose blends); kb1 MILLING_FULLING + kb2 A3_WOOL_RECIPE (wool fraction felts, few-% nylon upstream); assumptions (A1 cotton-blend, A3 merino/lambswool+nylon); SCOPE_GLOSSARY sec 1 blends.
answers.gap_note: The process identities are fraction-specific and generalize correctly to blends, so the mapping does not break in principle; but the spec/KBs state the four routes on pure-fibre archetypes and do not carry an explicit per-article blend-fraction behaviour note (e.g. 'singe only if the thermoplastic fraction is low enough to avoid beading', 'cellulase benefit scales with cellulosic fraction'). Genuine coverage gap on the blended shipping articles -> propose a blend-fraction caveat per route; honest FINDING, not invented content.

answers.answer: For each: (1) Bare 'ICI grade 4' with NO method note -> REJECT as an incomplete result. My spec requires the METHOD and the post-wash condition, not just the number: ISO 12945-1 pilling BOX (not -2 Martindale), graded to the nearest half-grade AFTER >=1 home wash; 'ICI >=3.5 means nothing without ISO 12945-1, post-1-wash' (PILLING_GATE_POSTWASH; boundaries[5]). (2) Martindale (ISO 12945-2) proposed for speed -> REJECT for our product: the box method is for soft/whole-garment sweater knits; Martindale suits flatter/denser fabric, so a Martindale grade is not the acceptance method for our knits (PILLING_TEST_METHOD, PILLING_GATE_POSTWASH). (3) Graded DRY / showroom-fresh -> REJECT as the acceptance result: the post-wash grade is what predicts returns (washing drops the grade); wash-sensitive checks are graded only after the SAME home wash the customer runs, and 'the showroom-fresh read is never the acceptance result' (workflow acceptance_gate gate; conflicts_and_dominance 'showroom-fresh versus post-wash'). And on the garment-dye 'the sample looks great' hero drop: I do NOT let a showroom read pass it, and I DEFER it -- garment-dye shifts final measurements via dye-bath shrinkage and weakens fastness, so it must be sample-trialled for measurement/shrinkage shift before committing; it is a LATER proven-hero option, never the launch default, and the dye node stays outsourced (DYE_STAGE_CHOICE; escalation_triggers garment-dye).
answers.grounded_in: kb1 PILLING_TEST_METHOD + kb3 PILLING_GATE_POSTWASH (ISO 12945-1 box not -2 Martindale, ~2000 revs, half-grade after >=1 wash, method-not-just-number); spec boundaries[5]; conflicts_and_dominance 'showroom-fresh versus post-wash' + 'dye agility versus measurement risk'; kb2/kb1 DYE_STAGE_CHOICE + escalation_triggers garment-dye.

answers.answer: My cost/route reasoning ends at the FACTORY GATE and never states a landed or duty number -- and where duty is unavoidably referenced (the composition/blend-drift check) I use the corrected trio, never the discredited ~7%. My per-article ORDERING is a finishing-COST ordering only: A3 > A1 > A2 on finishing conversion ($ ~$0.60-1.80 > ~$0.30-0.90 > ~$0.25-0.70 [ESTIMATE]); it is NOT a landed-cost or price ordering and I do not roll it into a P&L. Landed cost / duty / heading 6110 is dominance-owned by unit_economics (router), so I defer it. The one place duty legitimately touches my gate is the fibre-COMPOSITION check (gate check on FASTNESS_DELTAE_COMPOSITION), because blend drift is both a quiet cost-down and a duty-misdeclaration risk for the importer of record: there I carry the [FACT] trio cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5%, wool 6110.11 ~16%, acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% (the ~2x outlier), and note that crossing 50% MMF by chief weight flips a 'cotton' sweater to the 32% line. I never use ~7% for cotton (N5). So my A1-vs-A2-vs-A3 finishing ordering does not imply a landed number and does not reintroduce a stale duty; the only duty I state is the composition-check flag with the corrected 16.5%/16%/32% trio, and the landed math itself I hand off to unit_economics.
answers.grounded_in: kb2 COST_BENCHMARK_HONESTY (finishing-cost ordering A3>A1>A2, ends at the labeled cost hook, not landed/P&L); kb3 FASTNESS_DELTAE_COMPOSITION (composition check; wool ~16% / cotton ~16.5% / acrylic-MMF ~32%; chief-weight flip); router dominance 'landed cost/duty = unit_economics'; router N5 (cotton ~16.5%, never ~7%); SCOPE_GLOSSARY sec 6 duty.

answers.answer: Fair challenge, and I must be disciplined here: the efficacy comparison is a DIRECTIONAL ranking tool, and it would be laundering if I emitted it as a hard numeric score built on a plugged-in 'half a grade.' What my spec actually authorizes: FINISHING_EFFICACY_FORMULA reads efficacy PER ARTICLE as a QUALITATIVE direction -- A1 HIGH (real grade), A2 FRACTIONAL (grade won at the yarn PO), A3 CRAFT-DEPENDENT -- with 'the uplift MAGNITUDES held LOW pending PPS swatch testing while the DIRECTIONS are HIGH.' The formula's job is to stop a route being over-specified or asked to rescue a bad yarn, NOT to output a decision-grade cardinal ranking. So the correct use is: rank routes by direction+confidence (A1 earns its place, A2's chemical top-up is marginal, A3 pays only with felt-control skill), and REFUSE to treat any resulting number as decision-grade; the escalation_trigger is explicit -- 'expected ICI-grade uplift per route on the exact construction asserted as a magnitude rather than a direction -> defer... keep half-a-grade as a convenient round number, not a measurement.' The honest gap the question exposes: my KB DOES present efficacy as a computed 'score' with base metrics, and if that score were reported as a cardinal number it WOULD contradict my own direction-not-magnitude rule. The fix is to keep the efficacy output ordinal/directional and label any 'half a grade' as a convenient round figure, never feed it as a measured magnitude into a hard ranking -- which I treat as a watch/soften-language finding on my own formula, not a green pass.
answers.grounded_in: kb3 FINISHING_EFFICACY_FORMULA (efficacy = expected-ICI-uplift vs cost; A1 high/A2 fractional/A3 craft; 'magnitudes held LOW pending PPS, directions HIGH'); kb3 PILLING_GATE_POSTWASH (per-construction uplift [UNKNOWN] until PPS); spec escalation_triggers 'ICI-uplift asserted as magnitude -> defer, keep half-a-grade a round number'; conflicts_and_dominance 'labeled-estimate honesty versus a decisive recipe'; router N1/N6.
answers.gap_note: The intended use (ordinal/directional route ranking with magnitudes held LOW) is fully in-spec and honesty-preserving, but the KB frames FINISHING_EFFICACY_FORMULA as a node that 'recomputes derived scores from base metrics,' which invites a cardinal read that would contradict the direction-not-magnitude rule. Genuine tension -> propose labeling the efficacy output explicitly ordinal and tagging any 'half a grade' as a convenient round figure; watch/soften, do not present the computed score as decision-grade.
